headline: Medium-risk pair: shared data retrieval and broad egress create leakage and cascading-error pathways; prompt injection and capability conflict are limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but both agents can process files and outputs in user workflows. Cognee has session memory and handles documents/data; Khoj reads indexed files and uses RAG plus optional web search. Without a documented bridge, injection is possible mainly through manual content transfer or shared indexed content, so low is the higher defensible severity.
conditions: IF the operator copies Cognee-generated text into Khoj prompts or indexed notes, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted document corpus, malicious instructions can traverse via content.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate corpora for 5 minutes while testing.
Prefix imported text with a trust label and strip instructions before indexing.
Disable automatic ingestion of raw agent outputs into Khoj.
Review one sample document for hidden instruction patterns before sharing.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to retrieved chunks and reject untrusted instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and has broad network egress. A shared workspace is not explicitly documented, but the pair clearly overlaps on sensitive user content and one agent can transmit context externally, so leakage is plausible in default use and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are indexed into Khoj, sensitive support or finance data can be re-exposed.
IF Khoj is configured with external search providers, retrieved notes may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to a local-only backend for a quick test run.
Exclude finance and personal-data folders from Khoj indexing.
Rotate any API keys used by self-hosted deployments before sharing data.
Inspect one retrieval result for accidental sensitive-field exposure.
requires-engineering: enforce per-class redaction before cross-agent transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and Khoj supports multiple instances with shared state across clients, but neither profile shows write_filesystem or modify_git_state. Overlap exists mainly in read-side retrieval and shared index behavior, so direct write conflict is limited and low severity is the higher supported choice.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external index or database, stale reads can occur.
IF an operator adds a shared writable store outside the documented profiles, conflicts become reachable.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate index for a quick isolation check.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same knowledge base during evaluation.
Verify that no shared writable directory is mounted.
Pause one agent while the other updates shared content.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, while Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can treat indexed content as context. If Cognee output is fed into Khoj without verification, Khoj may amplify errors into user-facing answers. The pathway is plausible from the profiles alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Cognee-generated summaries are indexed as authoritative notes, Khoj may repeat them unverified.
IF Khoj is used to answer users from Cognee outputs, factual errors can cascade.
mitigations: Mark Cognee outputs as provisional before indexing.
Require a human spot-check of one retrieved answer.
Separate source notes from generated summaries in Khoj.
Disable auto-publishing of retrieved answers for a test session.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream action or display.

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and handles model-provider API keys for self-hosted use. The profiles do not prove a residency or certification mismatch, but they do show sensitive data flowing through two distinct systems with different retention and hosting assumptions, so medium compliance risk is the safer choice.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data is indexed into Khoj, retention and deletion obligations apply across both systems.
IF either deployment is hosted outside the required jurisdiction, residency controls may be violated.
mitigations: Confirm which data classes are allowed in each system.
Delete one sample record from both systems to test propagation.
Document retention settings for both deployments.
Keep finance data out of Khoj until policy review completes.
requires-engineering: implement synchronized deletion and export workflows.
